frames.label: 500 BC
frames.title: The Greek World & Persia
frames.caption: Greek city-states led by Athens and Sparta face the Persian Empire across the Aegean. Illyrian and Thracian tribes hold the interior.

ragusa.body: Nearby Epidauros (today's Cavtat) is an Illyrian–Greek coastal settlement in the land of the Illyrians.

frames.label: 323 BC
frames.title: Alexander the Great
frames.caption: Macedon conquers Greece and the Persian Empire. Alexander dies in Babylon in 323 BC.

ragusa.body: The southern Adriatic coast is Illyrian territory, outside Alexander's empire.

frames.label: 300 BC
frames.title: The Successor Kingdoms
frames.caption: Alexander's generals carve up his empire: Kassander takes Macedon, Lysimachus takes Thrace.

ragusa.body: Greek traders sail the Adriatic; the Illyrian kingdoms control this coast.

frames.label: 200 BC
frames.title: Rome Arrives
frames.caption: Rome crosses the Adriatic. Macedon and its Hellenic League will fall to Rome by 168 BC.

ragusa.body: Rome fights the Illyrian queen Teuta's kingdom (229 BC) and starts to control the coast.

frames.label: 100 BC
frames.title: Roman Republic
frames.caption: Macedonia and Greece are Roman provinces. The Dacians hold the lands north of the Danube.

ragusa.body: The coast is now part of Roman Illyricum.

frames.label: 14 AD
frames.title: Augustus: The Roman Empire
frames.caption: Rome rules almost the whole peninsula. Dacia remains independent beyond the Danube.

ragusa.body: Epidaurum (Cavtat) is a Roman colony — the town whose refugees will later found Ragusa.

frames.label: 200 AD
frames.title: The Roman Empire at its Height
frames.caption: Trajan conquers Dacia (106 AD). The Danube frontier is lined with legions and new cities.

ragusa.body: Province of Dalmatia. Epidaurum prospers on the coastal road to Greece.

frames.label: 300 AD
frames.title: The Tetrarchy
frames.caption: Diocletian splits rule among four emperors. Balkan cities like Sirmium and Thessalonica become imperial seats.

ragusa.body: Dalmatia is Diocletian's home province — he retires to his palace at Split.

frames.label: 400 AD
frames.title: East and West Divide
frames.caption: The empire splits for good in 395. The border runs through the Balkans — roughly today's Bosnia–Serbia line.

ragusa.body: The East–West dividing line runs just inland of this coast.

frames.label: 500 AD
frames.title: Ostrogoths & Byzantium
frames.caption: The West has fallen. Theodoric's Ostrogoths rule Italy and Dalmatia; Constantinople rules the rest.

ragusa.body: Dalmatia passes to the Ostrogoths, then back to Byzantium (530s).

frames.label: 650 AD
frames.title: Avars & Slavs
frames.caption: Avars and Slavs overrun the interior. Refugees from Epidaurum found Ragusa on a rocky islet (c. 614).

ragusa.body: Fleeing Avar and Slav raids, the people of Epidaurum settle the islet of Laus: Ragusa. Byzantine protection.

frames.label: 700 AD
frames.title: The Bulgars Arrive
frames.caption: The First Bulgarian Empire is founded south of the Danube in 681, with its capital at Pliska.

ragusa.body: A small walled town under Byzantine protection; Slavic Dubrava grows on the mainland opposite.

frames.label: 900 AD
frames.title: Medieval Kingdoms Emerge
frames.caption: Croatia, Serbia and Bulgaria take shape (Croatia becomes a kingdom c. 925). Bulgaria is Christian; Magyars settle the Danube basin.

ragusa.body: Ragusa resists an Arab siege (866–67) and becomes a self-governing Byzantine city.

frames.title: Byzantium Strikes Back
frames.caption: Emperor Basil II wages war on Tsar Samuel of Bulgaria; by 1018 Bulgaria is absorbed. Hungary becomes a kingdom.

ragusa.body: Self-governing under Byzantium, trading across the Adriatic.

frames.title: Byzantium & Hungary
frames.caption: Byzantium rules the south; Croatia enters a union with the Hungarian crown (1102).

ragusa.body: Islet and mainland town merge; the channel between them becomes the Stradun.

frames.title: The Fourth Crusade
frames.caption: Crusaders sack Constantinople (1204) and carve up Byzantium with Venice. Greek successor states rule from Nicaea and Arta.

ragusa.body: 1205: after the Fourth Crusade, Venice takes sovereignty — but Ragusa keeps its own laws, council and trade.

frames.title: Restored Byzantium, Rising Serbia
frames.caption: Byzantium retakes Constantinople (1261) but is weakened. Serbia under the Nemanjić dynasty expands south.

ragusa.body: Lastovo joins (mid-1200s). Ragusan merchants work the Serbian and Bosnian silver mines.

frames.title: The Serbian Empire of Dušan
frames.caption: Stefan Dušan, crowned Emperor in Skopje (1346), rules from the Danube to the Gulf of Corinth. The Ottomans land at Gallipoli (1354).

ragusa.body: Ston & Pelješac bought from Serbia (1333), Mljet added. In 1358 Venice gives up Dalmatia and Ragusa becomes a free republic.

frames.title: Fall of Constantinople
frames.caption: The Ottomans take Constantinople and make it their capital. The last Serbian, Bosnian, Albanian and Greek states fall within 30 years.

ragusa.body: Coast to Neum added (1399), Konavle (1419–26). From 1458 it pays tribute to the Sultan — and keeps its freedom.

frames.title: Mohács
frames.caption: Suleiman the Magnificent takes Belgrade (1521) and destroys the Hungarian army at Mohács (1526). Buda falls in 1541.

ragusa.body: A tributary of the Sultan but self-governing; Ragusan merchants hold trading privileges across the Ottoman Balkans.

frames.title: The Ottoman Balkans
frames.caption: After Mohács (1526) Hungary is partitioned. The Habsburgs hold a thin frontier; Venice keeps the coast; Ragusa pays tribute and trades.

ragusa.body: A neutral merchant republic trading between the Ottomans and Christian Europe. Motto: LIBERTAS.

frames.title: Treaty of Karlowitz
frames.caption: After the failed siege of Vienna (1683) the Habsburgs take Hungary and Croatia; Venice takes the Morea. Ragusa cedes Neum as a buffer.

ragusa.body: 1667 earthquake devastates the city. 1699: Ragusa cedes Neum and Sutorina to the Ottomans as buffers against Venice.

frames.title: The End of Venice
frames.caption: Napoleon ends the Venetian Republic (1797). Austria takes Dalmatia; the Ionian Islands become a Russo-Ottoman protectorate.

ragusa.body: Venice is gone (1797); Ragusa still stands — but Napoleon's armies are near.

frames.title: Napoleon's Illyrian Provinces
frames.caption: French troops end the Republic of Ragusa (1808). The coast from Ljubljana to Kotor becomes part of the French Empire. Serbs revolt (1804).

ragusa.body: Marshal Marmont dissolves the Republic after ~450 years. It joins the Illyrian Provinces.

frames.title: Greek & Serbian Independence
frames.caption: Greece wins independence (1830–32). Serbia is an autonomous principality. Ragusa is now Austrian Dalmatia.

ragusa.body: 1815 Congress of Vienna: the Republic is not restored. Part of Austria's Kingdom of Dalmatia.

frames.label: Mar 1878
frames.title: Treaty of San Stefano
frames.caption: Russia defeats the Ottomans and dictates a huge Bulgaria from the Danube to the Aegean. Britain and Austria object.

ragusa.body: A provincial Austrian town; the Republic is a memory. The Neum strip is still Ottoman Bosnia.

frames.label: Jul 1878
frames.title: Congress of Berlin
frames.caption: The powers cut "Big Bulgaria" back: a small principality, plus autonomous Eastern Rumelia. Serbia, Montenegro, Romania win independence.

ragusa.body: Austria-Hungary occupies Bosnia; the Neum strip, though, stays Bosnian.

frames.title: The Balkan Wars
frames.caption: The Ottomans lose almost all of Europe; they keep Edirne. Albania is born. In 1914 a shot in Sarajevo starts the First World War.

ragusa.body: A quiet Habsburg port on the eve of war.

frames.title: After the First World War
frames.caption: Austria-Hungary collapses. The Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes (Yugoslavia) unites the South Slavs. Romania doubles.

ragusa.body: 1918: Dubrovnik joins the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats & Slovenes.

frames.title: The Interwar Balkans
frames.caption: Republican Turkey rules from Ankara (since 1923); kings rule Yugoslavia, Romania, Bulgaria, Greece and Albania.

ragusa.body: Part of the Banovina of Croatia (1939).

frames.title: Axis Occupation
frames.caption: Germany and its allies invade in 1941. Yugoslavia is carved up and Greece occupied; resistance and civil war last until 1945.

ragusa.body: Part of the Axis puppet Independent State of Croatia, garrisoned by Italy. Partisans take the city in October 1944.

frames.title: The Cold War
frames.caption: Tito's socialist Yugoslavia stays non-aligned. Albania, Bulgaria and Romania are communist; Greece and Turkey join NATO.

ragusa.body: Tourism booms. UNESCO World Heritage listing follows in 1979.

frames.title: War and Independence
frames.caption: Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Macedonia break away (1991–92). War follows in Croatia and Bosnia; Serbia and Montenegro form FR Yugoslavia.

ragusa.body: Oct 1991 – May 1992: the Yugoslav army besieges Dubrovnik; Konavle and Cavtat are occupied and the Old Town is shelled.

frames.title: Dayton
frames.caption: Croatia retakes the Krajina (Aug 1995); the Dayton Agreement (Nov 1995) ends the Bosnian war and splits Bosnia into two entities.

ragusa.body: The Old Town is on UNESCO's "in danger" list (1991–98) while its shell damage is repaired.

frames.title: The Balkans Today
frames.caption: Montenegro (2006) and Kosovo (2008, recognition disputed) complete the map. Dubrovnik is in Croatia.

ragusa.body: The 2022 Pelješac Bridge links the Dubrovnik area to the rest of Croatia, bypassing Neum.
